issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers class defines a method named appendElement(T[] array, T element), but the template's Stock class (and the solution) call ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). This name mismatch causes a compile-time error and prevents students from building and running the project. Students will be unable to use the provided Stock.addToStockIngredients implementation as-is because the referenced helper method does not exist in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper method names consistent. Either rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...), or change the calls in Stock (and other classes) to use appendElement(...). Aligning the method name across template and solution will resolve the compilation issue while preserving the exercise's intent.

issues.description: The helper method for appending an element to an array is referred to with different identifiers across artifacts: the template's ArrayHelpers defines appendElementToArray(...) but the template's Stock and the solution's ArrayHelpers use addElementToArray(...). This mismatch (appendElementToArray vs addElementToArray) refers to the same conceptual utility and will confuse students and cause compilation errors when they try to use the provided helper methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Rename the template ArrayHelpers.appendElementToArray(...) to addElementToArray(...) (or change all callers to use appendElementToArray(...)). Ensure the ArrayHelpers method name used in Stock (ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray) matches the actual method in ArrayHelpers so students can directly use the provided helper methods without confusion.
